questions.correct_answer: The additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of a good.
questions.explanation: Marginal cost (MC) specifically refers to the change in total cost resulting from producing one additional unit. It's a key concept in understanding a firm's production decisions.
options: The cost of all fixed inputs.
The additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of a good.
The average cost per unit produced.
questions.question: A firm's marginal cost is the additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of a good.

questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. In this case, -10% / 5% = -2.0. A value greater than 1 (in absolute terms) indicates elastic demand.
questions.question: If the quantity demanded of a product decreases by 10% when its price increases by 5%, what is the price elasticity of demand?

questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is determined by opportunity cost, not absolute cost. A country should specialize in producing goods where it has the lowest opportunity cost, even if it's not the most efficient producer in absolute terms.
options: More efficiently in terms of labor hours.
questions.question: A country has a comparative advantage in producing a good if it can produce that good at a lower opportunity cost than another country.
